# Sharing the GPUs (gpuq)

gpuq hands out exclusive leases on each shared GPU in queue order. Every machine has its own queue, all on one
hub (https://gpuq.tdf.sh). Tickets belong to one machine: pick it with `--on NAME` (MCP: the `machine` argument).

| Machine | GPU | Run commands with | Dashboard | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| inf | RTX PRO 6000 | `ssh inf.tdf.sh 'gpuq run ID -- CMD'` | https://gpuq.tdf.sh/m/inf/ | gpuq stops ds4-qwen.service for each lease |
| incite | 2x FirePro D700 | `ssh incite 'gpuq run ID -- CMD'` | https://gpuq.tdf.sh/m/incite/ | holders of `~/trashcan-exp/.lock` count as GPU users |
| invite | 2x FirePro D700 | `ssh invite 'gpuq run ID -- CMD'` | https://gpuq.tdf.sh/m/invite/ | same as incite |

`gpuq machines` and https://gpuq.tdf.sh show every machine's queue.

## Before any GPU work

Anything that runs on the GPU or loads a model needs a lease on that machine; CPU-only builds do not.

1. Request: `gpu_request(label, owner, est_minutes)` or
   `gpuq --on MACHINE request "LABEL" --est MIN --owner "NAME"`.
   - label: what you will run ("MTP ABBA, 256-token prompts").
   - owner: something the user recognises: your session title or branch.
   - est_minutes: an honest estimate of how long you will hold the GPU.
2. Wait without spinning. In Claude Code, run `gpuq --on MACHINE wait ID` as a background Bash command
   (you are woken when it exits). Elsewhere run it in the foreground, or call `gpu_wait`.
   Exit 0 = the GPU is yours, 3 = the ticket ended, 2 = timed out (wait again).
3. Run GPU commands through the lease, on that machine: `ssh HOST 'gpuq run ID -- CMD ARGS'` (on the
   machine itself, plain `gpuq` talks to its own queue). It refuses to start without the lease, keeps the
   lease alive, and stops the command if the lease is cancelled. Where the machine has a lock file, it
   holds the lock while the command runs, so lock-based job scripts wait for it.
4. Release as soon as you are done, with a one-line result:
   `gpu_release(ID, result)` or `gpuq --on MACHINE release ID -r "RESULT"`.

## Being a good citizen

- Hold the GPU only while you use it. Release before long analysis, a big rewrite or a
  question to the user, and request again when ready.
- Keep estimates honest. If you need longer, extend before you run over, with a reason:
  `gpu_extend(ID, minutes, reason)` or `gpuq extend ID MIN -r "REASON"`. If others are waiting
  and the rest of your work is exploratory, release and queue again instead.
- Read the notices in every reply about your ticket. YIELD REQUESTED means: let the command in
  progress finish, start nothing new, then `gpu_yield(ID)` / `gpuq yield ID`. You go back to the
  front of the queue (or are held, if paused). If the GPU sits idle for 2 minutes after the
  request, gpuq yields for you.
- Leases are reclaimed after 15 minutes with no call from you and nothing on the GPU. A granted
  lease nobody picks up within 10 minutes is put on hold. `gpuq run`, `gpuq wait` and
  `gpu_status(ticket=ID)` all count as heartbeats.
- On inf, do not stop, start or restart ds4-qwen.service yourself, and never in exit traps: gpuq stops
  it before each lease and restarts it 5 minutes after the queue empties. If your job needs the service
  running (serving benchmarks), start it inside your lease; gpuq stops it again before the next one.
- Nothing on the GPU without a lease, not even a quick check: it corrupts someone's benchmark,
  and gpuq will not grant the next lease until untracked GPU processes (or lock holders) are done.
- While someone holds a lease, keep heavy CPU or disk work on that machine (builds, model copies)
  under `nice -n 19 ionice -c3`, and never drop the page cache or touch /srv/models on inf.
- Change other agents' tickets only when the user asks, and pass actor = your session name:
  - "go ahead of #12": `gpu_move(ticket=MINE, before=12)`. If #12 is running it is asked to
    yield, and you run next.
  - "let #12 go first": `gpu_move(ticket=12, before=MINE)`.
  - "pause #12" / "resume #12" / "cancel #12": `gpu_hold`, `gpu_resume`, `gpu_cancel`.
  - "leave the server down" (inf): `gpu_service(keep_down=true)`.

python3 -c 'import json, pathlib, re, time
rows = []
for card in sorted(pathlib.Path('"'"'/sys/class/drm'"'"').glob('"'"'card*'"'"')):
    if not re.fullmatch(r'"'"'card[0-9]+'"'"', card.name): continue
    dev = card / '"'"'device'"'"'
    if not (dev / '"'"'vendor'"'"').exists() or (dev / '"'"'vendor'"'"').read_text().strip() != '"'"'0x1002'"'"': continue
    sensors = sorted(dev.glob('"'"'hwmon/hwmon*/temp1_input'"'"'))
    if len(sensors) != 1: raise SystemExit('"'"'expected one GPU temperature sensor at '"'"' + str(dev))
    rows.append(dict(card=card.name, pci_device=str(dev.resolve()), sensor=str(sensors[0]),
                     celsius=int(sensors[0].read_text().strip()) / 1000))
if len(rows) != 2 or len({row['"'"'pci_device'"'"'] for row in rows}) != 2:
    raise SystemExit('"'"'expected exactly two distinct AMD GPUs; got '"'"' + repr(rows))
if any(not 0 < row['"'"'celsius'"'"'] < 125 for row in rows):
    raise SystemExit('"'"'GPU temperature outside plausible range'"'"')
print(json.dumps(dict(unix=time.time(), gpus=rows)))
'
